traveller_stance: Takes the watch. Walks with the waggons. Leaves when the roads part.
topic_prose_hint: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

npc_attitude: The master deals fast and keeps looking back down the road while he does it.
concrete_content: He will sell food cheap and pay for a sword to walk with them tonight, because he has seen the same three men behind the caravan since the last river crossing.
tension: He is buying protection and calling it a trade. Both of them can see the men on the road.
traveller_stance: Takes the coin. Walks at the rear. Watches the three men.
topic_prose_hint: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

npc_attitude: A single trader with a mule and a professional smile that does not quite reach the eyes.
concrete_content: Salt, thread, a whetstone and a small pot of honey at slightly too high a price, with good road-news thrown in to justify the margin.
tension: He is honest enough and he will still take whatever the market allows. The news is the real value and he knows it.
traveller_stance: Pays a little over. Takes the news. Notes the mule is better shod than the man.
topic_prose_hint: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

npc_attitude: Frank and hard-worn; she names what she has and what she needs in the same breath.
concrete_content: Dried fish, a bed in the byre and the new line of the crossing since the storm shifted the sandbanks, for salt and word from the north.
tension: She trades from a position of knowing more about this country than anyone he will meet today and she prices accordingly.
traveller_stance: Gives the northern news. Takes the crossing. Does not haggle over the fish.
topic_prose_hint: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

npc_attitude: Mountain-folk of the White Mountains: courteous, slow to warm, and unwilling to let a stranger go up the pass unprepared.
concrete_content: Ewe-cheese, a coil of good rope and a stick cut to the right length for the scree, given for whatever he thinks fair — and a flat statement of which hour of the day the pass is safe.
tension: They have carried bodies down off that pass. The rope is not a courtesy.
traveller_stance: Takes the rope and the stick. Goes up at the hour they name.
topic_prose_hint: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

npc_attitude: No ceremony at all. Gear is put out on a stone: take what is needed, leave what is not.
concrete_content: A cache opened — arrows, a spare cloak, hard bread, a phial of athelas — and the current state of the circuit given in six sentences.
tension: Between those who keep the same watch there is no bargaining, only accounting. The cache will be restocked by whoever passes next.
traveller_stance: Takes only what he will use. Says what he has left behind him for the next man.
topic_prose_hint: Have them speak of loyalty to king and folk, and the binding weight of a word once given.

npc_attitude: Fellow travellers on the same road, willing to pool what they have because the night is coming either way.
concrete_content: A shared fire, a shared pot and watches split between them, plus everything they know about the next two days of road.
tension: Nobody is in charge of this arrangement and it works precisely because nobody asks anything beyond the morning.
traveller_stance: Puts his rations into the pot. Takes the second watch. Parts from them at the crossroads.
topic_prose_hint: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

npc_attitude: River-folk mending nets who talk while their hands keep working.
concrete_content: Fresh fish, a place on the jetty out of the mud and a warning that the water has been running wrong for a week — up when it should be down.
tension: The river is their whole living and something upstream has changed. They would like a traveller who is going that way to look.
traveller_stance: Eats the fish. Agrees to look upstream. Does not promise to come back.
topic_prose_hint: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

npc_attitude: Courteous and unhurried. The offer is made as though it had been decided long before he arrived.
concrete_content: Waybread, clean water and a night under a hythe of woven branches, with the road ahead described exactly: three fords, two of them safe, and the hour at which the last of them can be crossed.
tension: Nothing is asked in return, which is itself a kind of weight. The gift assumes he will do something worth the giving.
traveller_stance: Accepts without protesting. Asks one question, well chosen.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: Kind, but the kindness has a limit set into it, and the limit is spoken plainly.
concrete_content: They will heal what can be healed tonight, feed him, and set him on a path that skirts the bad country; they will not go with him past the eaves of the wood.
tension: They have judged that his road is his own and are unwilling to be drawn along it. The help is real; the boundary is not negotiable.
traveller_stance: Takes the healing. Accepts the boundary without argument.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

npc_attitude: They look at him longer than is comfortable before anything is offered, and what is offered is aimed at something other than his hunger.
concrete_content: Food, and then a request that he sit while one of them sings over him — for the weariness they say is not only in his legs.
tension: They can see what he is carrying and they are treating it, not discussing it. He may refuse, and refusing will cost him the night's rest.
traveller_stance: Sits for it. Does not ask what they saw in him.
topic_prose_hint: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

npc_attitude: Greeted as one of the old alliance — a formality observed exactly, with real warmth somewhere under it.
concrete_content: Bread, cord, arrows fletched their way, and word of which of the two northern passes has been quiet this month and which has not.
tension: They deal with the Dúnedain as inheritors of an old agreement. He is being helped as an heir, not as a man.
traveller_stance: Gives the greeting in Sindarin. Takes the arrows. Reports what the north looks like from his side.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: The courtesy is thinner than usual. Something has made them careful with the roads and with who is on them.
concrete_content: They will provision him for four days and ask him to change his line of march: the valley he intended is being watched, and they would rather he did not walk into what they are watching it for.
tension: They are asking him to alter his errand for reasons they will not explain. They expect him to accept it on trust alone.
traveller_stance: Takes the provisions. Changes the line. Files the fact that they would not say why.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

npc_attitude: Recognition and immediate deference, and then the ordinary business of kin looking after kin.
concrete_content: A proper camp made for her without being asked, hot water, and news of who has passed west along this road in the last hundred years.
tension: They assume she is going west eventually. Nobody says so. The assumption sits in the middle of the conversation.
traveller_stance: Accepts the camp. Answers about the road. Does not confirm the assumption.
topic_prose_hint: Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.

npc_attitude: Gentle and slightly too careful with her, the way people are careful with something they have been told about.
concrete_content: They offer shelter, a horse if she wants one, and an escort as far as the river — and one of them asks whether she is travelling by choice.
tension: The question is kindly meant and lands somewhere she does not want examined tonight.
traveller_stance: Refuses the escort. Takes the horse. Does not answer the question.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: Grave, quiet hospitality, offered by people who have understood something without being told it.
concrete_content: A fire built low, food she does not want, and a place made ready in the middle of their camp rather than at its edge — deliberately, so that she is surrounded.
tension: They have decided she should not be left alone tonight. They will not say that either.
traveller_stance: Lies down where they made the place. Says nothing about why it was made there.
topic_prose_hint: Have them bring up an age-old loss — a drowned realm, a kinsman long dead — as though it were last night.

npc_attitude: Formal, practical and faintly amused at how badly Men travel — they begin repacking his gear before asking permission.
concrete_content: Waybread and a small flask of cordial, a strap replaced, a wound cleaned properly, and the safe line down to the Ford of Bruinen given landmark by landmark.
tension: This is a household that has been doing this for two thousand years. The help is routine to them and remarkable to him.
traveller_stance: Lets them repack it. Learns the landmarks by heart.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: Grave and busy. They are moving something along this road and the traveller has arrived in the middle of it.
concrete_content: They will treat his hurts and give him three days of food, and ask that he take the low road for the next two days and mention to nobody what he saw on this one.
tension: Their errand is larger than his and they are buying his silence with real kindness. It is not a threat and it is not free either.
traveller_stance: Accepts the terms. Takes the low road. Keeps it to himself.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

npc_attitude: Unseen until they choose otherwise; then grave, close-mouthed and exact about what is permitted.
concrete_content: Lembas-cake, a coil of grey rope and a flet to sleep on above the ground, on the condition that he does not walk the wood after dark and does not cut anything living.
tension: The gift and the rule are one thing. They are lending him their forest for a night on very specific terms.
traveller_stance: Sleeps where he is put. Cuts nothing. Leaves at the hour they name.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: Cheerful on the surface and entirely unyielding underneath. Wine appears before questions do.
concrete_content: A hot meal, a skin of strong wine and a guide as far as the forest gate, in exchange for word of the eastern road and how the river ran where he crossed it.
tension: They are generous within their bounds and they have no intention of letting him wander their wood unescorted.
traveller_stance: Drinks less than they pour. Gives the river honestly. Walks out where they lead him.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

npc_attitude: A company on the march halts for him, which is more than they were obliged to do.
concrete_content: Food from their own store, a lantern of the sort that is not lit with fire, and the road west laid out with the two places on it where a fire should not be built.
tension: They are going west and he is going the other way. Whatever they give him, they will not be here to see it used.
traveller_stance: Takes the lantern. Asks what is at the two places. Gets a straight answer.
topic_prose_hint: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

npc_attitude: A guardian of a border who has decided to help him leave rather than help him stay.
concrete_content: Water, dried fruit and a blunt instruction: the way he is going is closed, and here is the way that is not, and it costs him a day.
tension: The kindness is a means of moving him off ground they are keeping. He gains a safe road and loses a day, and that is the whole bargain.
traveller_stance: Takes the day's loss without arguing about it.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: Grey-clad and preoccupied, courteous in the manner of people whose real attention is on the harbour behind them.
concrete_content: Ship's bread, salt fish and passage across the firth in a boat going that way regardless, and news of which havens still keep a light.
tension: Everything here is arranged around departure. He is being helped on his way by people arranging their own.
traveller_stance: Takes the crossing. Does not ask when the next ship sails.
topic_prose_hint: Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.

npc_attitude: A single ranger of the green wood, spare with words, generous with practical things.
concrete_content: Arrows, a mended boot-sole and the exact position of the one clean spring in a day's march of bad water.
tension: He has been alone in the wood a long time and gives what is useful because that is the only currency he keeps.
traveller_stance: Takes the arrows. Marks the spring. Asks nothing about his errand.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

npc_attitude: An Elf of learning who would rather trade knowledge than goods, and says so at once.
concrete_content: Copies made of two road-maps, the true name of a ruin on his route and an hour of instruction on what the boundary-stones there mean — in exchange for a full account of what he has seen on the road.
tension: He wants the traveller's eyes and is paying properly for them. It is the most honest transaction of the journey.
traveller_stance: Gives a full and accurate account. Takes the maps. Learns the stones.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: Pale, quiet and utterly at home in the cold; they appear beside him without any sound of arrival.
concrete_content: A hot drink he cannot identify, dry wrappings for his hands, and the safe line across the ice, which is not the line the ground suggests.
tension: They are helping a traveller who would otherwise be dead by morning, and they are not sentimental about it.
traveller_stance: Drinks it. Follows their line and not his own judgement.
topic_prose_hint: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

npc_attitude: A fisher of the shore-folk, weathered and easy, who offers a place in the boat before any talk of payment.
concrete_content: Grilled fish, fresh water and a lift along the coast past the headland that cannot be walked around at this tide.
tension: The sea sets the terms here and the Elf simply knows them. He is being carried because walking would kill him.
traveller_stance: Takes the boat. Bails when told to. Leaves something at the shrine-stone on landing.
topic_prose_hint: Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.

npc_attitude: Ordinary to look at and entirely unsurprised to find him here, as though the meeting were on a list somewhere.
concrete_content: Food he did not know he needed, a name for the thing that has been troubling his road, and directions given by landmarks that turn out to be exactly right.
tension: The help is freely given and the terms are not explained. Something is being served that has nothing to do with him.
traveller_stance: Accepts it. Does not press for the reason.
topic_prose_hint: Have them offer aid on terms of their own — a gift, a path, a rescue — odd and not freely explained.

npc_attitude: Kindly and abstracted, and the kindness lands like a decision that was made about him rather than for him.
concrete_content: A hot meal, a night's shelter that should not exist where it is standing, and one piece of counsel that will only make sense in three days.
tension: He is being helped for reasons attached to something much larger than his journey. Refusing would be permitted and would cost him.
traveller_stance: Eats. Sleeps. Remembers the counsel word for word.
topic_prose_hint: Have them speak words that carry more than they say — a warning, a riddle, or counsel from one far older than he seems.

npc_attitude: Attentive in a way that is not comfortable, and the offer is made only after a long, weighing look.
concrete_content: A rescue, more or less: a way out of the country he has walked into, given on the single condition that he turns back now and does not go on to look.
tension: The condition is the whole of it. He can have the help or he can have the road. Not both.
traveller_stance: Weighs the condition. Chooses. Is not argued with either way.
topic_prose_hint: Have them put a strange, searching question that seems to weigh the traveller's worth or errand.

npc_attitude: A shabby brown-clad old man surrounded by too many birds, who talks to the traveller and to a hedgehog with the same courtesy.
concrete_content: Herbs sorted into twists of leaf with instructions for each, a warm mash of something wholesome, and a message about the road ahead delivered second-hand from a crow.
tension: He is entirely serious about the birds and the birds are entirely accurate. Taking him lightly is the only mistake available here.
traveller_stance: Takes the herbs. Believes the crow. Says thank you to both of them.
topic_prose_hint: Have them turn the talk to beasts, trees and growing things, and the keeping of them.

npc_attitude: Distracted, fussing over a hurt animal, and only half his attention on the traveller until something in the answers catches it.
concrete_content: He will physic the traveller and the traveller's blisters and then ask for help carrying an injured beast two miles out of the way to a place where it can be left safely.
tension: The detour is real and inconvenient and it is also the whole test, though he does not think of it as one.
traveller_stance: Carries the beast. Loses the two miles. Gets more than two miles of value back.
topic_prose_hint: Have them turn the talk to beasts, trees and growing things, and the keeping of them.

npc_attitude: Absurdly cheerful, singing more than speaking, and entirely unbothered by anything the traveller might be afraid of.
concrete_content: Yellow cream, honeycomb, bread and butter, a bed of dry rushes and a rhyme to call by if the ground turns treacherous — none of it asked for, none of it refusable.
tension: The gift is total and the terms are nonsense and the nonsense works. His country, his rules, and the rules are kind.
traveller_stance: Eats far too much. Sleeps like the dead. Learns the rhyme.
topic_prose_hint: Have them offer aid on terms of their own — a gift, a path, a rescue — odd and not freely explained.

npc_attitude: Booming and hospitable, and once or twice startlingly serious for about four words at a time.
concrete_content: A night's lodging, all the food he can hold, his gear dried by morning, and directions out of the forest that only work if followed exactly and without cleverness.
tension: He will give everything and explain nothing. What he says about the willow and the barrows is not a story and should not be treated as one.
traveller_stance: Follows the directions exactly. Does not improve on them.
topic_prose_hint: Have them speak words that carry more than they say — a warning, a riddle, or counsel from one far older than he seems.

npc_attitude: Greets her by a name in a tongue older than her father's house, and then offers her breakfast as though that were the greater matter.
concrete_content: Bread, honey and yellow cream, and a remark made in passing about the water under the Downs that is worth more than any map she has been given this year.
tension: He is older than her grief and treats it as weather. It is the first time in a long while that nobody has been careful with her.
traveller_stance: Eats. Laughs, which surprises her. Notes the remark about the water.
topic_prose_hint: Have them offer aid on terms of their own — a gift, a path, a rescue — odd and not freely explained.

npc_attitude: Nothing appears. The offer arrives as a road that has become easy, a wind at his back, a door standing conveniently open.
concrete_content: Everything he needs is suddenly available on the eastern line of march: water, shelter, dry wood, an unguarded track. Only the eastern line.
tension: This is not generosity. It is a hand on the small of his back, and the destination is not his.
traveller_stance: Notices how easy it has become. Breaks off eastward travel and pays for the harder road.
topic_prose_hint: Have them offer aid on terms of their own — a gift, a path, a rescue — odd and not freely explained.

npc_attitude: A courtesy without a body: the dread lifts, briefly, in exchange for nothing that can be named.
concrete_content: Rest is offered — real rest, the first in weeks — if he will sleep in a particular place, on ground that some old instinct says has been chosen for him.
tension: The bargain is being made with the part of him that is tired, not the part that decides. That is the whole method.
traveller_stance: Refuses the ground. Sleeps badly somewhere worse and wakes up himself.
topic_prose_hint: Have them turn the talk to the great shape of things: the slow war against the Shadow, and each one's small part in it.

npc_attitude: Startled, then polite, then talkative once it is clear nothing is going to be demanded of them.
concrete_content: Where the next farm is, whose dog to avoid, how bad the rain was last week and how good the plums will be if it holds off — delivered in one breath.
tension: There is nothing at stake for them beyond politeness, and politeness is taken very seriously.
traveller_stance: Answers the plum question properly. Is remembered kindly for it.
topic_prose_hint: Have them share who said what to whom, and the small scandals and rumours of the country round.

npc_attitude: Polite and plainly wishing the conversation elsewhere; one keeps a hand on the gate the whole time.
concrete_content: They will confirm the road and mention, reluctantly, that strangers came through nine days ago and did not behave like traders.
tension: They do not want to be involved in whatever this is. Saying it out loud is already more than they meant to do.
traveller_stance: Takes the road. Does not ask them to describe the strangers twice.
topic_prose_hint: Have them show polite unease at strangers and the wide world, wishing adventures would happen elsewhere.

npc_attitude: Frightened and stubbornly courteous anyway, which is a thing hobbits can do that almost nobody else manages.
concrete_content: They have moved the children to the far farm and they are not saying why; they ask only whether the road east is passable, and press a wrapped seed-cake on him.
tension: They are more afraid than they will admit and the cake is what they have instead of words.
traveller_stance: Takes the cake. Answers about the road honestly, gently.
topic_prose_hint: Have them offer food, a tale or directions, with homely, unsuspecting goodwill.

npc_attitude: Brown, small and immediately at ease once the traveller sits down, which lowers him to a reasonable size.
concrete_content: Talk of the burrow, the state of the bank it is dug into, whose mushrooms are whose, and a warning about the ditch further on that has swallowed a pony.
tension: Nothing here is dangerous and nothing here is trivial to them. The ditch is the most important news in the district.
traveller_stance: Sits down. Listens about the ditch. Avoids the ditch.
topic_prose_hint: Have them chatter about their hole, their garden, their kin and the doings of the next farm over.

npc_attitude: Bolder than the rest of their kind and openly delighted to have found somebody new to interrogate.
concrete_content: Questions about where he has been, in order, with follow-ups — and in exchange the whole gossip of the district and an offer to walk part of the way for the novelty of it.
tension: Their curiosity outruns their caution. Somebody in that family is going to leave home eventually.
traveller_stance: Answers the easy questions. Deflects one. Lets them walk a mile.
topic_prose_hint: Have them share who said what to whom, and the small scandals and rumours of the country round.

npc_attitude: Broad, slow-spoken river-folk who go on with their work while they talk and do not look up much.
concrete_content: Which channel takes a boat and which takes a leg, where the eels are running, and the fact that the reeds have been cut on the far bank by somebody who does not live there.
tension: They notice everything on this water and mention about a third of it.
traveller_stance: Asks about the cut reeds. Gets a longer answer than expected.
topic_prose_hint: Have them share who said what to whom, and the small scandals and rumours of the country round.

npc_attitude: Barely willing to be seen — the talk happens across ten feet of bracken and could end at any moment.
concrete_content: Two sentences about where the water is good and one about a place further on where the birds have gone quiet, and then they are finished with him.
tension: They live out here precisely to avoid conversations like this one. Every word is a concession.
traveller_stance: Keeps his distance. Thanks them once. Lets them go.
topic_prose_hint: Have them show polite unease at strangers and the wide world, wishing adventures would happen elsewhere.

npc_attitude: On the road with a pack far too big for him and pathetically glad of company at the fire.
concrete_content: Where he is from, where he thinks he is going, and a request for an honest opinion on whether the eastern road is as bad as people say.
tension: He has no idea how far he actually is from home. Telling him the truth might turn him around, which would be the kindest outcome.
traveller_stance: Tells him the truth about the road. Shares food. Does not laugh at the pack.
topic_prose_hint: Have them talk of the next meal, good ale, a warm fire and a soft bed — the real business of life.

npc_attitude: Stops, looks him over from boots to hood, and gives a greeting that is closer to a receipt than a welcome.
concrete_content: Where the road is bad, where the water is good, and a flat refusal to say where he himself is going or what is under the oilcloth on the pony.
tension: Everything he offers is accurate and nothing he withholds will be prised out. That is the whole shape of the exchange.
traveller_stance: Trades road for road. Does not look at the oilcloth twice.
topic_prose_hint: Have him put short, suspicious questions, saying little of his own roads and liking prying even less.

npc_attitude: Short with him, and it is not personal — something on this road has already annoyed him and the traveller is merely next.
concrete_content: A complaint about a toll being taken at a crossing where no toll was taken last year, with the exact sum, the exact place and the exact name of the man taking it.
tension: He wants a witness more than he wants sympathy. The grievance will be repeated in front of the right people eventually.
traveller_stance: Notes the name and the crossing. Agrees the toll is theft. Moves on.
topic_prose_hint: Have him bring up a grievance nursed for generations — a slight, a debt, an enemy not yet repaid.

npc_attitude: Grim and abrupt, with the shoulders of someone who has been walking fast for days and would rather not explain why.
concrete_content: He says one useful thing and one dark one: the eastern gallery road is closed, and whatever closed it did not do it with tools.
tension: He has decided to give the warning and not the story. The story is his folk's business and not the traveller's.
traveller_stance: Takes the warning. Does not ask him to elaborate.
topic_prose_hint: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

npc_attitude: Names what he has, names what he wants for it, and stands there until an answer comes.
concrete_content: Iron rations, a decent whetstone, a strap-buckle and a mended boot-nail, priced fairly and not one copper below it.
tension: He will not haggle and he will not cheat, and he considers the second a matter of honour and the first a waste of daylight.
traveller_stance: Pays the named price. Gets full value. Learns not to bargain with him.
topic_prose_hint: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

npc_attitude: Deals warily and keeps the pack between them while he does it.
concrete_content: He will trade food and a place at his fire for the traveller standing the first watch, because he has not slept properly since the pass and will not say what is behind him.
tension: He needs someone else's eyes for four hours and he hates needing it. The trade is an admission he will not make in words.
traveller_stance: Takes the watch. Wakes him only if it matters. Does not mention the pass.
topic_prose_hint: Have him put short, suspicious questions, saying little of his own roads and liking prying even less.

npc_attitude: Blunt to the point of rudeness and entirely without deference, which is the closest thing to respect he offers anyone.
concrete_content: He will give her food and the road-notes she needs, and wants in exchange the correct old name of a landmark on his map, which nobody alive has been able to give him.
tension: He is not awed by her age; he is interested in it, which is rarer and easier to bear.
traveller_stance: Gives him the old name. Takes the road-notes. Appreciates being asked as a source rather than a wonder.
topic_prose_hint: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

npc_attitude: Well-armed, well-provisioned and openly proud of both; the greeting is loud and the questions are practical.
concrete_content: News of the eastern road, the price of iron three markets away, and an unprompted opinion on the folk of the Long Lake that lasts some time.
tension: They have nothing to fear on this road today and it shows in how much they are willing to say.
traveller_stance: Lets him talk. Keeps the price of iron. Does not comment on the Lake-men.
topic_prose_hint: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

npc_attitude: Closed as a shut door on the subject of where he is from, and grimly talkative about everything else.
concrete_content: He wants to know whether anyone has been up the Dimrill Stair this season, and who, and whether they came back down it.
tension: He is asking about a doorway his folk lost long ago and will not say why he is counting the people who go near it.
traveller_stance: Answers what he saw. Does not ask what he is planning.
topic_prose_hint: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

npc_attitude: Business-like, unhurried, and visibly pleased to have found a customer this far from a market.
concrete_content: Salt, nails, a good knife and a length of chain, sold at market price plus carriage, with the state of the Great Road thrown in at no charge.
tension: This is a trading party and he is a small piece of a long ledger. The fairness is professional, not sentimental.
traveller_stance: Buys the knife. Takes the road-news. Pays the carriage without complaint.
topic_prose_hint: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

npc_attitude: A merchant who has the goods unpacked before agreement is reached, because he knows what a tired man looks at first.
concrete_content: Boot-nails, a spare buckle, hard biscuit, and a small mirror he is oddly determined to sell; and news of every market between here and the mountains.
tension: He is going to make a profit and be entirely honest about how much. The mirror is a matter of professional pride by now.
traveller_stance: Buys the biscuit and the nails. Refuses the mirror twice. Buys the mirror.
topic_prose_hint: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

npc_attitude: Suspicious on sight — a man alone near his diggings is a claim-jumper until proved otherwise.
concrete_content: Short questions about which way the traveller came and whether he stopped anywhere near the stream-head, and a grudging note on where the ground is safe to walk.
tension: He is standing on a find he has not registered with anyone and he is not subtle about guarding it.
traveller_stance: Answers plainly. Shows no interest in the stream-head. Walks where he is told to walk.
topic_prose_hint: Have him put short, suspicious questions, saying little of his own roads and liking prying even less.

npc_attitude: A patrol that halts him with a raised axe-handle and then talks to him quite civilly from behind it.
concrete_content: They want his name, his road and whether he has seen anyone moving on the high tracks; in return they will say which of the two gates is open this month.
tension: They are keeping a border and he is a data point. The civility is real and so is the axe-handle.
traveller_stance: Gives name and road. Names what he saw on the high tracks. Uses the open gate.
topic_prose_hint: Have him speak of loyalty to king and folk, and the binding weight of a word once given.

npc_attitude: Half-wild and hard to place, speaking a rough Westron and watching the traveller's hands rather than his face.
concrete_content: He trades furs and worked bone, wants iron above everything, and mentions that the northern ice has been giving up things this year that were better left under it.
tension: He is used to being taken for something less than he is and has stopped minding. The remark about the ice is not a joke.
traveller_stance: Trades iron for the furs. Takes the remark seriously.
topic_prose_hint: Have him put short, suspicious questions, saying little of his own roads and liking prying even less.

npc_attitude: Filthy, cheerful and glad of any face that has not been underground for a month.
concrete_content: A hot meal at the mine-mouth, water, and a lantern refilled, in exchange for news from outside and a hand at the windlass for an hour.
tension: They are lonely, well-fed and slightly bored, and company is worth more to them than the lamp-oil.
traveller_stance: Turns the windlass. Eats their food. Gives them every scrap of news he has.
topic_prose_hint: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

npc_attitude: Standing across the road with the easy confidence of men who have done this before and not been punished for it.
concrete_content: They want a toll for a bridge they did not build, and they are prepared to call it a toll for as long as he is prepared to call it one.
tension: Nobody has drawn yet. What happens next depends on whether he looks like more trouble than a few coins are worth.
traveller_stance: Pays the coin or refuses it, and either way keeps his hands where they can be seen.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: Four of them spread across the way in a formation that closes as soon as he stops walking.
concrete_content: They want the pack opened and the contents named, and they have already decided which items they will be keeping.
tension: The positions were taken before he arrived. Talking is still possible; walking away is not.
traveller_stance: Names the contents. Gives up what is replaceable. Does not turn his back.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: No demand at first — only silence and a slow closing of the distance, which is worse.
concrete_content: They are not after goods. They want to know who he is and who sent him, and one of them keeps checking his face against something he has been told.
tension: This is not robbery. Someone is looking for someone and he resembles the description closely enough.
traveller_stance: Answers the first question and not the second. Chooses the ground he will stand on.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

npc_attitude: Ragged, hungry and dangerous in the specific way of men with nothing left to lose and no discipline to lose it with.
concrete_content: They want the pack, the boots and the water, in that order, and they are arguing among themselves about the boots while they say it.
tension: They are badly organised and there are five of them. The disorganisation is the opening and it will not last.
traveller_stance: Marks the one who is actually leading. Speaks only to him.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: Better armed than bandits should be, and two of them still wearing pieces of a uniform they have not bothered to remove.
concrete_content: They demand a toll and give a garrison's name while doing it, and are visibly uncertain whether the traveller will know that the garrison disbanded two years ago.
tension: They are deserters trading on an authority they no longer have. Naming that out loud would end the pretence and start something else.
traveller_stance: Lets the pretence stand. Pays the false toll. Remembers the uniforms.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: Two in front talking pleasantly while a third moves round to where he cannot comfortably watch.
concrete_content: A friendly conversation about the road, whose only purpose is to keep his eyes forward for the count of twenty.
tension: The talk is the weapon here. Answering it politely for too long is how travellers lose their packs.
traveller_stance: Steps sideways so all three are in front of him. Keeps talking pleasantly.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: Not hostile so much as inconvenienced: he has walked into the middle of something and now they must decide what to do about him.
concrete_content: They want to know what he saw at the landing, and they are willing to buy an answer of none at all, in coin, on the spot.
tension: Nobody wants a fight here. They want a witness who is either paid or gone, and they are offering him the choice.
traveller_stance: Takes the coin or refuses it plainly. Does not pretend not to understand the offer.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: Perfectly polite, unarmed to look at, asking questions in an order that is far too well constructed to be casual.
concrete_content: He wants the traveller's name, his last three stopping-places and the name of anyone who vouched for him, and he already knows two of the answers.
tension: This is an interrogation dressed as a courtesy. Every answer is being checked against something written down elsewhere.
traveller_stance: Gives true answers that reveal nothing. Notices which questions he does not ask.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

npc_attitude: Spears grounded but held, and the speaker stands close enough that the conversation cannot be a long one.
concrete_content: This ground is claimed, the claim is older than any map he is carrying, and they want to hear him say that he is only passing through.
tension: They are not looking for plunder. They are looking for an acknowledgment, and they will take it in words if he offers them.
traveller_stance: Says the words. Means them. Walks the line they point out.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: Chariot-folk of the eastern plains, unhurried, treating the encounter as a matter of administration rather than violence.
concrete_content: They want tribute — a weapon, a beast, or a day of labour — and they have a formula for it that has been used on this road for generations.
tension: Refusal is permitted and has a known price. They will not be insulted by it; they will simply apply the price.
traveller_stance: Chooses which tribute to pay. Does not attempt to negotiate the formula.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: Horsemen who circle once before anyone speaks, and the speaking is done from the saddle at a distance.
concrete_content: They demand to know whose service he is in, and the question has only two answers they accept, and neither of them is none.
tension: They cannot place him and they dislike what cannot be placed. The wrong answer here costs more than the pack.
traveller_stance: Answers in a way that gives them a category to file him under. Keeps walking west.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: Disciplined and unhurried, in the manner of men who are part of something much larger and know it.
concrete_content: An officer asks for his road and his purpose through a translator, and writes the answers down, which is worse than if he had shouted them.
tension: He is being recorded, not robbed. Whatever he says here will be somewhere in a file by the next full moon.
traveller_stance: Gives a plain and unremarkable account of himself. Does not embellish it.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

npc_attitude: Tall, courteous and entirely cold; the courtesy is the frightening part, since it costs them nothing to maintain it.
concrete_content: He is asked, in excellent Westron, what his lineage is — and it is clear from the phrasing that the answer matters more to them than his errand.
tension: They are the inheritors of a specific old treason and they can hear the North in his speech. The politeness will last exactly as long as it is useful.
traveller_stance: Answers about his lineage as little as courtesy allows. Gives nothing they can use.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: A checkpoint where no checkpoint should be, manned by men who serve something they do not name aloud.
concrete_content: They demand papers that were never issued in this country, then a name, then an account of the last four days — and they are hoping he lies about one of them.
tension: The demands are designed to produce a false answer they can act on. There are six of them and one road.
traveller_stance: Tells the plainest possible truth about the four days. Gives them nothing to catch.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

npc_attitude: Come up from a beached boat, loud and quick, and dealing in threats because threats have always been cheaper than work.
concrete_content: They want whatever is in the pack and any coin on him, and they want it before whoever else is on this shore arrives.
tension: They are in a hurry, which makes them dangerous and also makes them stupid. The hurry is the lever.
traveller_stance: Gives them the coin. Keeps the pack. Lets the hurry do the arguing.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: Desperate rather than wicked, blocking the path with a stick and a shaking voice and no plan at all beyond stopping him.
concrete_content: They want food and they are asking for it in the worst possible way, because asking properly has not worked twice already this week.
tension: There is no real threat in it and there is real danger anyway: cornered people do things they did not intend.
traveller_stance: Puts food on the ground and steps back. Does not draw.
topic_prose_hint: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

npc_attitude: They come out onto the road in a spread line and start with noise, because noise has worked for them before.
concrete_content: Demands to know what he carries, mixed with jeering about what they will do with him afterwards, and no interest at all in the answers.
tension: There is no negotiation available here. The talk is only the space before the rush.
traveller_stance: Says nothing. Picks the ground. Watches the flanks rather than the loud one.
topic_prose_hint: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

npc_attitude: They hold the way with the confidence of a company that has been given orders about this road.
concrete_content: The one in charge wants him alive and says so, and the others are audibly unhappy about that instruction.
tension: The order to take him alive is the only thing keeping this a conversation, and their discipline is thin.
traveller_stance: Uses the argument between them. Does not answer any question directly.
topic_prose_hint: Have them bicker and turn on one another over loot, orders or who eats first, overheard by the traveller.

npc_attitude: A rabble that stops short when it realises he has not run, and covers the hesitation with shouting.
concrete_content: Threats, a demand for his gear, and an argument breaking out at the back over who will take his boots.
tension: They are more numerous than brave and they know exactly how the count stands. The shouting is to keep their own nerve up.
traveller_stance: Stands still. Lets the argument at the back get louder. Chooses a moment.
topic_prose_hint: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

npc_attitude: Mounted on wargs, circling wide, and the beasts are less patient than the riders.
concrete_content: No demands worth the name — only the shape of a hunt being arranged around him while one of them talks to keep his attention forward.
tension: Every second spent listening is a second they use to close the circle. The wargs will decide the timing, not the riders.
traveller_stance: Stops listening. Gets his back to something solid.
topic_prose_hint: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

npc_attitude: Two of them only, and they are as unhappy to be seen as he is to see them.
concrete_content: A snarled demand that he turn back the way he came, which is the first thing they have said that they actually mean.
tension: They are scouts and a fight will bring attention neither side wants. There is an ugly little deal available here.
traveller_stance: Considers turning back. Decides what the road ahead is worth.
topic_prose_hint: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

npc_attitude: One of them steps forward and speaks in a Westron far too correct, and the others go quiet for it.
concrete_content: He asks the traveller three questions that are not about the road at all — about a name, a date and a place — and he is patient about waiting for answers.
tension: This is not a patrol. Something is being confirmed, and the questions themselves say more than any answer would.
traveller_stance: Refuses all three. Notes exactly what was asked.
topic_prose_hint: Have them fling harsh demands at a captive — who are you, who sent you, what do you carry — backed by the lash.

npc_attitude: A column halted on the road, and the challenge comes as a matter of procedure from men and orcs who have somewhere else to be.
concrete_content: An officer demands the road be cleared and the traveller kneel while the column passes, and gives him about four seconds to decide.
tension: He is an obstruction on a military road. Dignity is expensive here and the price is fixed.
traveller_stance: Kneels or does not, and lives with the choice while the column goes by.
topic_prose_hint: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

npc_attitude: Man-shaped enough to pass in poor light and openly enjoying the moment when the traveller works out that they are not men.
concrete_content: A toll demanded in the manner of ordinary brigands, with the language slipping into something else halfway through.
tension: They trade on being mistaken for men and they resent it at the same time. The resentment is the dangerous part.
traveller_stance: Does not comment on what they are. Deals with them exactly as he would with brigands.
topic_prose_hint: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

npc_attitude: A laden column halts, and the challenge is bad-tempered rather than eager: they are carrying cargo and do not want the delay.
concrete_content: Snarled orders to get off the road and stay off it until the last cart has passed, with threats attached but no real appetite behind them.
tension: They want him gone, not dead. Whatever is on those carts matters more to them than he does.
traveller_stance: Gets off the road. Counts the carts. Sees what is on them.
topic_prose_hint: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

npc_attitude: Disciplined, silent and in armour that fits, which is the worst sign of all. Nobody jeers.
concrete_content: One question, asked once, about what he is doing on this road — and then they wait, and the waiting is not a bluff.
tension: These are not raiders. There is no confusion to exploit and no argument among them to use.
traveller_stance: Answers or does not. Understands that this time the choice is the whole of it.
topic_prose_hint: Have them fling harsh demands at a captive — who are you, who sent you, what do you carry — backed by the lash.

npc_attitude: Greets him first, which is unusual, and the greeting is exactly as long as it needs to be.
concrete_content: A remark about the season that turns out to be a warning about the river, and a question about where he slept last night that is not idle.
tension: They are deciding, in the space of four sentences, whether he is the sort of traveller this country needs fewer of.
traveller_stance: Answers about where he slept. Hears the warning inside the remark.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: Appears at the edge of the path without any of the usual noise of arrival, and does not come closer.
concrete_content: A short, unfriendly enquiry about his business under these trees, followed by one piece of information he badly needs about the trail ahead.
tension: They do not like strangers in the wood and they dislike deaths in it more. The help is given grudgingly and given.
traveller_stance: States his business briefly. Does not step off the path.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: Courteous in an older, heavier fashion, and something in the phrasing belongs to a country that no longer exists.
concrete_content: He speaks of the land as it was before the coast changed, then corrects himself to the present, and the correction is the saddest part of the exchange.
tension: He has been in these lands since before the first Men walked them and is not entirely living in this century.
traveller_stance: Lets the older name stand without correcting it. Listens.
topic_prose_hint: Have them bring up an age-old loss — a drowned realm, a kinsman long dead — as though it were last night.

npc_attitude: Formal, precise and faintly distant, as though the conversation were being conducted from further away than it appears.
concrete_content: A question about what Men are saying in the west this year, asked with genuine interest and a slight air of collecting specimens.
tension: The interest is real and the distance is real. Both are permanent features.
traveller_stance: Answers accurately. Resists the urge to perform.
topic_prose_hint: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

npc_attitude: Sea-grey and easy-mannered, with the particular calm of people who measure time in tides rather than years.
concrete_content: Talk of the weather turning, of a wreck on the sand two winters back, and of a light kept on a headland further along the shore that is worth walking to.
tension: Nothing is urgent to them. The information is still exactly what he needs.
traveller_stance: Asks about the light. Walks to it.
topic_prose_hint: Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.

npc_attitude: Speaks from ten paces away, in a Westron worn thin from lack of use, and does not close the distance at all.
concrete_content: A warning that the ice on the inlet is a week from breaking and a question about whether he has seen fires in the north.
tension: They speak to almost nobody and this exchange costs them something. It is being spent on purpose.
traveller_stance: Answers about the fires. Takes the ice seriously.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

npc_attitude: Easier to talk to than most of their kin, and quicker to ask the sort of question a mortal would ask.
concrete_content: Ordinary road-talk conducted with unusual attention, and one question about how long he means to keep walking roads like this one.
tension: The question is asked by someone who has had to make a choice about mortality, or will have to, and it lands harder than intended.
traveller_stance: Answers honestly. Does not ask them the same thing back.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: Charming in a way that does not fit the place or the hour, and the charm does not reach the eyes at all.
concrete_content: He offers an easy road, a shorter way and pleasant company for it, and every detail he gives about the country is subtly wrong.
tension: Something in this one broke a long time ago. The errors are not ignorance and the courtesy is bait.
traveller_stance: Declines pleasantly. Does not take the shorter way. Does not turn his back on the parting.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: Two of them, already knowing his name from somewhere, and unwilling to say from where.
concrete_content: They tell him what is on the road two days ahead and ask him to describe, exactly, what he passed at the ruin behind him.
tension: They are running a border and he has walked through part of it. The trade of information is not optional so much as obvious.
traveller_stance: Describes the ruin precisely. Accepts that they will not say how they knew his name.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

npc_attitude: A patrol on old business, armoured, correct, and in no mood for a long conversation with anyone.
concrete_content: A brisk warning that the northern shore of the lake is not to be walked this month, delivered as an order and not a suggestion.
tension: They are the last remnant of something and they hold their small piece of country absolutely. He is not being asked.
traveller_stance: Takes the southern shore. Does not test the order.
topic_prose_hint: Have him speak of loyalty to king and folk, and the binding weight of a word once given.

npc_attitude: Walking west alone and glad enough of a word on the road, in the manner of someone who has already left everything else behind.
concrete_content: Where the road runs from here to the sea, which houses on it are still keeping their doors, and how few of them there are now compared with the last time this journey was made.
tension: He is going to the harbour and will not be coming back. Nothing about the conversation is heavy and everything in it is final.
traveller_stance: Walks with him a while. Does not ask why now.
topic_prose_hint: Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.

npc_attitude: Immaculate courtesy that manages to make the traveller aware of every stain on his cloak without a word being said about it.
concrete_content: Formal questions about his road and his errand, and an answer about the state of the country that is more useful than the manner suggests.
tension: The condescension is unconscious and the information is excellent. Taking offence would cost him the second thing.
traveller_stance: Answers formally. Takes the information. Lets the manner pass.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

npc_attitude: Grave and welcoming at once, and clearly used to Men — the greeting is pitched for a mortal ear.
concrete_content: News of the havens, the state of the coast road, and a mention that fewer ships come to their quay each decade and none of them are new.
tension: They have lived beside Men for an age and are the last of their kin who do. The friendliness is genuine and elegiac.
traveller_stance: Gives them the news they ask for. Notices what is not said about the quay.
topic_prose_hint: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

npc_attitude: Green-clad and half-invisible until they speak; the voice arrives before the shape resolves.
concrete_content: A statement that the wood is not what it was, given as a fact about the trees rather than a complaint, and a route that avoids the worst of it.
tension: They are the oldest kind of woodland folk and they measure the sickness of a forest in centuries. This year is worse than last.
traveller_stance: Follows the route. Believes the diagnosis.
topic_prose_hint: Have them turn the talk to beasts, trees and growing things, and the keeping of them.

npc_attitude: Veiled against the sun and formally polite, with a courtesy that has rules he does not know.
concrete_content: Talk of water — where it is, who owns it, what it costs — and a question about whether the northern wells are held by anyone this season.
tension: Water is the only real subject here and he is being assessed as a competitor for it.
traveller_stance: Answers about the wells. Observes the courtesy without pretending to understand it.
topic_prose_hint: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

npc_attitude: Cautious, sun-dark and quick to end the conversation if it turns to anything official.
concrete_content: Where the next cistern is, and a flat statement that the tax-riders came through eleven days ago and took more than the tally allowed.
tension: They are being squeezed by their own overlords and a stranger is the safest possible audience for saying so.
traveller_stance: Takes the cistern. Does not repeat what he heard to anyone in a uniform.
topic_prose_hint: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

npc_attitude: Talkative traders of the wine-country, immediately friendly and immediately calculating.
concrete_content: The price of wine three markets downriver, the state of the eastern road, and an offer to carry a letter for him if he is going the other way.
tension: Everything is business and the business is pleasant. There is no hidden edge to this one.
traveller_stance: Gives the road-news. Sends no letter. Buys nothing and is liked anyway.
topic_prose_hint: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

npc_attitude: Hard-faced hill-men who stop him with a question rather than a weapon, which is itself a decision.
concrete_content: They want to know whether he came through the valley by the standing stone, and whether anyone was camped there when he did.
tension: There is a feud running in these hills and his answer places him in it whether he wants to be placed or not.
traveller_stance: Answers only what he saw. Refuses to guess whose camp it was.
topic_prose_hint: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

npc_attitude: Curious rather than hostile; a young one is sent forward to talk while the others watch from the slope.
concrete_content: Questions about where he comes from and what he is carrying, asked plainly, and a warning about the herd of something large moving north of here.
tension: The youth is being tested by his own people and the traveller is the test. Both of them know it.
traveller_stance: Answers the boy seriously. Gives him something to carry back.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

npc_attitude: Loud, cheerful and already halfway through a story that started before he arrived.
concrete_content: News from three ports, a wildly exaggerated account of a storm, and one entirely accurate detail about a captain who is hiring.
tension: Nine parts noise and one part gold, and the gold is the hiring. Sorting them is his problem.
traveller_stance: Lets the story run. Keeps the name of the captain.
topic_prose_hint: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

npc_attitude: Correct, bored and thorough — a patrol going through a procedure it has performed four hundred times.
concrete_content: Name, road, purpose, and then, unprompted, a genuinely useful warning about the state of the bridge and where the last robbery on this stretch happened.
tension: The procedure is dull and the men are decent. The warning is not part of their orders.
traveller_stance: Answers all three questions. Thanks them for the part that was not official.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

npc_attitude: Appears out of ground that looked empty, speaks quietly, and is plainly annoyed that the traveller is walking this line at all.
concrete_content: A short, exact account of what is ahead, and an instruction to be off this ground by dusk and not to light a fire on it.
tension: They are watching something and he is interfering with the watching. The information is given to move him along faster.
traveller_stance: Is off the ground by dusk. Does not light a fire.
topic_prose_hint: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

npc_attitude: Recognition on both sides within two sentences, and then the conversation becomes very economical.
concrete_content: Where the roads are watched, which house will still open its door, and a name that has stopped appearing on the circuit reports.
tension: Two people who keep the same kind of faith, comparing ledgers on a road neither of them will describe to anyone else.
traveller_stance: Trades the ledger honestly. Marks the missing name.
topic_prose_hint: Have him speak of loyalty to king and folk, and the binding weight of a word once given.

npc_attitude: Serene, footsore and entirely unworried about anything the traveller might be worried about.
concrete_content: Where the shrine-stones are on this road, which spring is thought to be blessed and which is only clean, and an offer to share bread on the strength of nothing at all.
tension: There is no calculation in it, which is rare enough on this road to be worth a moment of suspicion and then of shame.
traveller_stance: Shares the bread. Asks about the stones. Stops suspecting.
topic_prose_hint: Have them offer food, a tale or directions, with homely, unsuspecting goodwill.

npc_attitude: Town-bred, brisk and less interested in him than in whether the road he came by is fit for a waggon.
concrete_content: The market days in the next three towns, the current price of grain, and a complaint about the tolls that is at least half accurate.
tension: Purely transactional and quite friendly with it. He is a source of road conditions and nothing more.
traveller_stance: Answers about the waggon road. Keeps the market days.
topic_prose_hint: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

npc_attitude: Guarded and tired, in the manner of people who live in a town that used to matter and now mostly floods.
concrete_content: Which of the causeways still carries a man, what the bridge-works are charging this month, and a request that he not mention having come from the north side.
tension: Their whole living depends on the crossing and the crossing is failing. Strangers from the north are a subject with history.
traveller_stance: Uses the good causeway. Says nothing about the north side.
topic_prose_hint: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

npc_attitude: Gracious from horseback, with an attendant who does the practical parts of the conversation.
concrete_content: A courteous enquiry about his road, an invitation to make use of a well on their land, and a piece of political news he was not supposed to hear.
tension: The courtesy is genuine and the news was a mistake. Whether it was a mistake is worth thinking about later.
traveller_stance: Accepts the well. Files the news. Does not react to it.
topic_prose_hint: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

npc_attitude: Brief, unbothered and standing far enough back that the wind carries most of the words away.
concrete_content: Where the ice is thin, where the seals are, and a warning that the weather will turn within the day whatever the sky is currently doing.
tension: They speak to strangers rarely and never at length. Everything said is chosen for its usefulness.
traveller_stance: Believes the weather warning over his own eyes. Moves.
topic_prose_hint: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.
